task.description: WF-03 Step 3c IDIOM/SCOPE GATE for ISS-0427, hard blocking gate before TEST-DESIGNER. Independently verify: idiom/quality of test/support/tenant_template.ex as production-quality test infrastructure, SQL-injection surface from schema-name interpolation, scope discipline against production tenant_provisioning.ex and against ISS-0423, whether the :replay opt-out ever silently degrades from :clone on failure, the parity assertion's actual runtime cost and whether it is wired into a hot path, decision-record consistency, honesty of the reported 2.0x/1.8x performance claim, and test-coverage judgement for TEST-DESIGNER.

result.summary:
VERDICT: PASS, with one MAJOR finding that TEST-DESIGNER (not ELIXIR-DEV) must close, and two MINOR findings. This is not a rubber-stamp: I re-derived every claim below directly (git diff, real mix compile/format, a real test-file run, a real DB inspection) rather than trusting either ELIXIR-DEV handoff's narrative.

1. IDIOM AND QUALITY (test/support/tenant_template.ex, 1294 lines -- larger than the dispatch's '~600 lines' estimate, but the extra length is the 13-dimension parity module, not padding; read in full). Matches this codebase's established test-support idiom exactly: plain module, not a GenServer, not added to lib/letflow/application.ex's supervision tree -- same shape as Letflow.TenantFixture and Letflow.TenantSchemaReaper. Raw Repo.query!/2 for dynamic DDL against schema-qualified names is not a crutch here -- it is the SAME idiom lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex and lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex already use in production code, because Ecto's query DSL cannot express dynamic CREATE SCHEMA/CREATE TABLE LIKE/ALTER SEQUENCE OWNED BY statements. Every function either returns :ok, raises ExUnit.AssertionError (matching TenantFixture.report_and_raise/3's convention), or returns a tagged {:error, {:clone_failed, reason}} tuple -- no bare exceptions leaking past the module boundary, no silently-swallowed errors. No dead code found: template_state/0's @type is informational-only per its own doc comment (consistent with design 2.1) and every private function is called from at least one path. The previously-reported N+1 (per-column pg_get_serial_sequence calls in recreate_sequences!/1, the mechanism's hot path) is fixed -- confirmed by reading recreate_sequences!/1 directly: one batched information_schema.columns-driven query for the whole schema, not one per table x column. HOWEVER: a second N+1 of the identical shape survives in check_sequences/2 (dimension #5 of the parity check, lines 807-843) -- it calls columns_in/2 per table then serial_sequence/3 (a fresh Repo.query! each) per column, TWICE (once per schema side). This was not caught by ELIXIR-DEV's own N+1 sweep because it only measured the CLONE mechanism's cost, not the (currently unwired, see finding 2) parity check's own cost. Filed as MINOR, not BLOCKER, because assert_clone_parity!/2 is not on the per-test hot path today (see finding 2) -- but it will become one the moment TEST-DESIGNER wires use site 1 (build-time self-check) or a CI-run use-site-2 test file exercises it repeatedly, at which point this N+1 has the same shape and severity as the one already fixed. Recommend TEST-DESIGNER or a follow-up batch dimension #5's column discovery the same way recreate_sequences!/1 was fixed, using the identical information_schema.columns-driven single query per schema side.

2. SQL STRING BUILDING / INJECTION SURFACE. Verified schema-name provenance at every interpolation site rather than assuming it: clone_schema is derived exclusively via TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1, which casts through Ecto.UUID.cast/1 first (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:166-171) -- a cast failure returns {:error, :invalid_tenant_id} before any string ever reaches a query, so clone_schema is always exactly "tenant_" <> 32 lowercase hex chars, never free-form caller input. table/column/conname/tgname values interpolated into ALTER TABLE/CREATE TRIGGER/CREATE SEQUENCE statements come from Postgres catalog queries (pg_constraint, pg_trigger, pg_proc, information_schema.columns) scoped to the template schema itself, which is built only from this repository's own reviewed migrations -- not externally controlled at any point in this path. The FK/trigger/function qualifier-rewrite (String.replace(def_sql, "tenant_template.", clone_schema <> ".")) is a plain, unquoted substring replace -- verified this is deliberate and CORRECT, not sloppy: design section 0.5 documents, and I independently confirmed by reading Postgres's own pg_get_constraintdef/pg_get_functiondef/pg_get_triggerdef output shape cited in that section, that these functions emit the schema qualifier UNQUOTED whenever the identifier needs no quoting, which 'tenant_template' never does -- a QUOTED search pattern (an earlier design revision's mistake, since corrected) would silently match nothing and turn the rewrite into a no-op, which is a materially worse defect than what shipped. The one theoretical residual risk this technique carries -- the substring 'tenant_template.' appearing inside a CHECK expression string literal, a comment, or a column/constraint name rather than as an actual schema qualifier -- was checked against the real migration set (grep across priv/repo/migrations/*.exs found zero occurrences of the literal string 'tenant_template' anywhere, which is expected since the template schema name is synthesized only at test time, never present in migration source) and is additionally caught structurally if it ever did occur: a corrupted definition would fail to execute as valid DDL (Repo.query! raises) or would produce a definition that mismatches on the next parity check. Not a silent-corruption path today. No injection surface found.

3. SCOPE CREEP / SCOPE DISCIPLINE. Confirmed via git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex: EMPTY diff -- zero bytes changed, independently re-verified (not inherited from either ELIXIR-DEV handoff's claim), so production provision_tenant_schema/1 and replay_migrations/2 are untouched exactly as design section 7 requires. The template build path (build_template!/0) deliberately calls the REAL, unmodified replay_migrations/2 against a throwaway Tenant/Registration row rather than adding a new public function to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex -- this is the correct minimal-surface choice, not scope creep, and keeps the 'zero lib/ diff' claim literally true rather than merely close. git diff main...HEAD --stat confirms the only non-handoff/non-design-doc files touched are test/support/tenant_template.ex (new) and test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (modified, +52/-8 lines) -- no migration file, no other lib/ file. ISS-0423's own scope (parallelism, async: true, Sandbox.mode) is untouched: grepped this diff for Sandbox.mode/ExUnit.Case async and found neither touched; the design's own section 1 states this as an explicit non-goal and the diff honors it. Confirmed no absorption.

4. TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE RISK / NO SILENT FALLBACK. Read provision_schema!/2 in test/support/tenant_fixture.ex directly (lines 333-348): it is a strict two-clause function head dispatch on the literal atoms :replay and :clone, with no third catch-all clause and no rescue that routes a :clone failure into the :replay path. On clone_tenant_schema!/1 returning {:error, reason}, provision_schema!(:clone, ...) calls report_and_raise/3 (the same helper the :replay path already uses on its own failures) and raises ExUnit.AssertionError -- it does not retry as :replay, does not log-and-continue, does not default to a degraded schema. This is a genuine, verified 'no silent fallback' implementation, not a claim taken on trust. The escape hatch (template: :replay) is caller-opt-in only, defaulting to :clone -- confirmed no test in the tree currently combines a non-default migration_source: option with the fixture's new :clone default (grepped every migration_source hit across test/; the only real fixture-adjacent one, test/letflow/tenant_provisioning_event_seed_test.exs, uses its own independent local provisioned_tenant/0 helper that never touches TenantFixture at all), so the documented 'clone path cannot serve migration_source' caveat is correctly stated but not currently live anywhere -- no test is silently broken by the new default.

5. THE PARITY ASSERTION'S COST -- MAJOR FINDING. Grepped the entire repository for assert_clone_parity! call sites: it is called from EXACTLY ZERO places in shipped code today. Design section 3.4 specifies two use sites -- (1) a build-time self-check inside ensure_template!/0 comparing the template against a second, independently replay_migrations/2-built reference schema, restricted to dimensions #1-6/#8-13, and (2) a permanent test/support/tenant_template_test.exs (TEST-DESIGNER's artefact, explicitly deferred, not a gap). Use site (2) being absent is expected and correctly deferred. Use site (1) is NOT correctly deferred -- it is claimed as already done and is not. test/support/tenant_template.ex:298-303's own comment reads: '# design section 2.3 step 3: assert the template's own table set and migration # version set are complete, THEN run the full parity self-check (design # section 3.4 use site 1) against a genuinely independent replay_migrations/2 # build.' template_self_check!/0's actual body (lines 303-334, read directly) does ONLY a table-set MapSet diff and a migration-version-set MapSet diff against the template's OWN schema -- it never builds a second reference schema, and it never calls assert_clone_parity!/2 at all. The comment describes behavior the code does not have. Consequence, stated precisely: (a) today, the 13-dimension check ELIXIR-DEV built, verified, and reported timing implications about runs in ZERO production code paths -- it is reachable only if a future test file calls it directly, so 'is it expensive per clone' (this task's own framing) is currently moot because it never runs per clone, only if/when a test explicitly invokes it; (b) the design's own section 11 acceptance-criteria table states 'Constraint parity must be ASSERTED, not assumed' is satisfied by 'assert_clone_parity!/2, wired to two real runnable use sites in section 3.4' -- that claim is presently FALSE for use site 1, and neither ELIXIR-DEV handoff flags this as a discrepancy against the design's own claim (the continued handoff's next_action says use site 1 is 'not yet exercised by CI', which understates the actual state -- the function is not merely unexercised, it is uninvoked by any code path, including the one whose own inline comment claims to invoke it). This is scoped as MAJOR, not BLOCKER, because it does not misrepresent working code as broken or vice versa in a way that would ship a defect silently -- the clone mechanism itself (steps 1-9 of do_clone/2) is independently correct and was proven non-vacuous by ELIXIR-DEV's own four tamper-and-detect proofs (FK drop, sequence-trap, trigger drop, cross-schema trigger) run manually against assert_clone_parity!/2 called directly from a throwaway script, not via any wired use site -- so the CHECK itself works, it is just not yet connected to anything that runs automatically. But it is a real design-conformance gap this gate exists to catch, and the misleading comment (claiming behavior that isn't there) is exactly the kind of stale/inaccurate in-code claim a future reader -- including a REVIEWER auditing later without this session's context -- would be misled by. FIX REQUIRED, routed to TEST-DESIGNER per the design's own division of labor (section 3.4 explicitly calls TEST-DESIGNER the owner of turning both use sites into real runnable code): (i) wire use site 1 into ensure_template!/0's build sequence -- build a second schema via the real replay_migrations/2 and call assert_clone_parity!/2 against it, restricted to dimensions #1-6/#8-13 exactly as design section 3.4 item 1 specifies; (ii) fix or remove the misleading template_self_check!/0 comment in the meantime (a one-line correction ELIXIR-DEV or TEST-DESIGNER can make trivially) so it accurately describes what the function does today; (iii) build test/support/tenant_template_test.exs per use site 2. Given use site 1 is template-build-time-only (runs once per BEAM VM/partition, not per clone, per design section 3.4 item 1's own text: 'Runs ONCE per template build, not once per clone -- its cost is amortized across every test in the run'), its cost is not a concern for the per-test hot path even once wired -- this finding is about design-conformance and an inaccurate comment, not about a hidden performance regression.

6. DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY. No docs/migration/decisions/ record found that this design contradicts -- grepped decisions/ for schema-per-tenant, Ecto migration, and sandbox/pool related records; none constrains how a TEST schema is materialised (as opposed to a production one), and design section 7's own scope statement (production path untouched) keeps this squarely inside test infrastructure, which is not decision-record-governed territory the way lib/letflow/ architecture is. SandboxPool relationship verified as complementary, not competing, by reading both modules directly: SandboxPool.provision_sandbox/2 still calls replay_migrations/2 (unchanged, confirmed via the empty tenant_provisioning.ex diff) to pre-provision its own pooled schemas -- TenantTemplate does not touch, wrap, or call SandboxPool anywhere (grepped, zero references either direction) and TenantFixture's :clone path is an entirely separate provisioning route from the pool. The design's own claim ('pool decides WHEN a schema is available, template decides HOW CHEAPLY one is made') holds as a description of two genuinely independent, non-overlapping code paths, not just as prose -- verified structurally, not merely quoted.

7. HONESTY OF THE PERFORMANCE CLAIM. Sanity-checked the reported 2.0x median / 1.8x average against what is knowable independently: the design's own section 10 (read directly) states its 2.5x figure was ISSUE-FIXER's bare-clone measurement (no FK/sequence/trigger fix-up) and explicitly hedges that a fresh full-mechanism measurement was not yet known at design time -- so 2.5x was never a promise the implementation was bound to hit, and reporting a real, lower, full-mechanism number (which necessarily pays for three MORE round trips than the bare-clone baseline: the FK re-add query, the batched sequence query, and the new trigger/function re-add queries) below that baseline is the expected, honest outcome, not a red flag. ELIXIR-DEV's explicit statement that a separately-observed 4.3x figure from an earlier, smaller 5-run block-structured probe was NOT used as the reported number, in favor of a larger 10-run interleaved comparison, is the methodologically correct call -- block-structured timing (all of A, then all of B) is more exposed to a shared-host load-drift confound between the two blocks than interleaving, and choosing the less-flattering, more-rigorous number over the more-flattering, less-rigorous one is exactly what 'no speculation' and honest reporting require. I did not re-run the 10-run timing myself (this host's load is not controlled between sessions and a fresh run would not be comparable to or falsify the original in any useful way), but the reported method is sound and the number is not inflated.

8. TEST COVERAGE JUDGEMENT FOR TEST-DESIGNER. Beyond the 13-dimension parity check itself (already proven non-vacuous for FK, sequence, AND trigger/function degradations via four real tamper-and-detect proofs quoted in ELIXIR-DEV's continued handoff, independently spot-checked by me via one additional live run: `mix test test/letflow/definitions/promotion_test.exs` against real Postgres -- 8 passed, exit 0, log confirms the :clone path actually executed via the LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE marker, not merely claimed), TEST-DESIGNER should build: (a) test/support/tenant_template_test.exs per design section 3.4 use site 2 -- clone a throwaway tenant, assert full parity across all 13 dimensions, this is the permanent regression test that makes 'constraint parity is asserted, not assumed' a standing CI fact rather than a one-time manual verification; (b) the use-site-1 wiring from finding 5 above, ideally with its own assertion that ensure_template!/0 actually raises if the self-check would fail (a deliberately-broken-template probe, matching the tamper-and-detect method already proven for the clone side); (c) a small regression test on provision_schema!/2's dispatch itself -- confirm template: :clone is genuinely the default with no explicit option (opts \\ []) and that template: :replay still produces a working schema via the original path, so a future edit cannot silently flip the default or remove the escape hatch without a test noticing; (d) NOT a bespoke SQL-injection test -- finding 2 above establishes the schema-name provenance is structurally safe (UUID-cast-derived only), so a test asserting 'a malicious tenant_id is rejected' would just be re-testing Ecto.UUID.cast/1, already covered elsewhere. Do not treat ELIXIR-DEV's own tamper-and-detect proofs (run via ad-hoc scratch scripts, not committed test code) as sufficient coverage on their own -- they are evidence the mechanism CAN be proven non-vacuous, not a substitute for the permanent test file that proves it stays that way.

CLEANUP PERFORMED: found and dropped stray probe-residue schemas (probe_clone, probe_tpl in letflow_dev; a stale tenant_template in letflow_test1) left over from earlier design/implementation passes, clone-before-template order, per this task's explicit instruction -- confirmed via `SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'probe%'` returning 0 rows afterward in letflow_dev. These were not created by this review session (I ran zero probes of my own beyond the one real, already-adopted test file above) -- they were residue this run's own design/implementation passes had claimed, but had not actually, fully cleaned up.

OVERALL: the clone mechanism itself -- the actual DDL sequence, the FK/sequence/trigger qualifier-rewrite technique, the no-silent-fallback dispatch, the scope discipline against production code and against ISS-0423 -- is sound, idiomatic for this codebase, and honestly measured. The one MAJOR finding is a design-conformance gap (use site 1 unwired, with a comment that inaccurately claims otherwise) that does not undermine the mechanism's own correctness but must not be inherited silently by TEST-DESIGNER as 'already done' -- it is next work, not finished work.

issues.title: assert_clone_parity!/2 is called from zero places in shipped code -- design section 3.4 use site 1 (build-time self-check inside ensure_template!/0, comparing the template against a second independently-built reference schema across dimensions #1-6/#8-13) is not wired, and template_self_check!/0's own inline comment (test/support/tenant_template.ex:298-303) inaccurately claims it runs 'the full parity self-check' when the function body only performs a table-set and migration-version-set diff against the template's own schema.
issues.description: Verified by reading template_self_check!/0 (lines 303-334) directly and grepping the whole repository for assert_clone_parity! call sites (matches found only in tenant_template.ex's own definition and the design doc's prose -- none in any calling code). Design section 11's acceptance-criteria table claims 'Constraint parity must be ASSERTED, not assumed' is satisfied by assert_clone_parity!/2 being 'wired to two real runnable use sites in section 3.4' -- true for neither use site today (use site 2, the permanent test file, is correctly and explicitly deferred to TEST-DESIGNER; use site 1 is claimed as done via an inaccurate code comment and is not). Not a correctness defect in the clone mechanism itself (ELIXIR-DEV's own four tamper-and-detect proofs, run via ad-hoc scratch scripts calling assert_clone_parity!/2 directly, demonstrate the check function itself works correctly for FK/sequence/trigger degradations) -- the gap is that nothing in the shipped, automatically-run code path invokes it yet. Route to TEST-DESIGNER: (1) wire ensure_template!/0 to build a second reference schema via replay_migrations/2 and call assert_clone_parity!/2 against it restricted to dimensions #1-6/#8-13, per design section 3.4 item 1's exact text; (2) correct or remove the inaccurate comment at tenant_template.ex:298-303 in the same change; (3) build test/support/tenant_template_test.exs per use site 2.

issues.title: check_sequences/2 (parity dimension #5, test/support/tenant_template.ex:807-843) has the same N+1 round-trip shape ELIXIR-DEV already found and fixed in recreate_sequences!/1's hot path, but the fix was not applied to the parity check's own sequence-discovery query -- one columns_in/2 call per table, then one serial_sequence/3 round trip per column per schema side.
issues.description: Not a hot-path defect today because assert_clone_parity!/2 is not yet wired into any per-clone or per-test-run path (see the MAJOR finding above) -- but it will become one the moment TEST-DESIGNER wires use site 1 or a CI-run use-site-2 test exercises this dimension repeatedly, at which point it has the identical shape and severity class as the N+1 that was measured to erase the entire clone-vs-replay speedup before being fixed. Recommend batching dimension #5's column/sequence discovery into one information_schema.columns-driven query per schema side, the same technique already proven in recreate_sequences!/1, when TEST-DESIGNER or a follow-up touches this dimension.

issues.title: test/support/tenant_template.ex is 1294 lines, roughly double the '~600 lines' the dispatch's own description estimated -- confirmed this is not padding or scope creep, just the true size of a correctly-scoped 13-dimension structural parity check plus the clone mechanism, but worth a standing note for whoever next estimates a module's size from a dispatch description rather than the design doc's own line-by-line specification.
issues.description: Read in full; every function maps to either a design section 2.3 mechanism step or a design section 3.2 parity dimension, with no unused/orphaned code found (template_state's @type is explicitly informational-only per its own doc comment, consistent with design section 2.1, and is the only module attribute without an active runtime use). Not routed as an issue since it is an estimate-accuracy note, not a defect.

result.next_action: Do NOT route to TEST-DESIGNER as a bare 'write tests' handoff -- route with this gate's MAJOR finding attached as required work: wire design section 3.4 use site 1 into ensure_template!/0 (with its own tamper-and-detect proof that a broken template actually raises), fix the inaccurate template_self_check!/0 comment in the same change, then build test/support/tenant_template_test.exs (use site 2) plus the three coverage items named in finding 8 above. Once that lands, this gate does not need to re-run from scratch -- a follow-up REVIEWER pass can scope itself to just the new wiring and the corrected comment, since every other finding in this handoff (idiom, injection surface, scope discipline, no-silent-fallback, decision-record consistency, performance-claim honesty) is a clean PASS on the code as it stands today and does not need re-verification unless touched.
